Server-rendered mustache pages (pages/layouts/partials/emails without engine: gotmpl) escape `{{var}}` for the context it lands in. Body text and ordinary attributes: HTML-escaped. Unquoted attribute values also escape spaces, `=` and backticks so a value cannot add attributes.

URL attributes (href, src, action, formaction, poster, srcset, xlink:href, cite, data, ...): a value whose URL would start with javascript:, vbscript: or a non-image data: scheme renders as `#blocked-unsafe-url`. http(s), mailto, tel, relative paths and data:image/png|gif|jpeg|webp|avif|bmp|x-icon stay as written. `srcdoc` values are escaped twice, so they show as text inside the frame instead of becoming its markup.

<script> (any JavaScript MIME type the browser runs - including legacy text/jscript, text/javascript1.x, text/x-ecmascript - module, application/json, ld+json, importmap) and on* event-handler attributes: inside a quoted string, template literal, regex or comment the value is JS-string escaped (\uXXXX for quotes, <, >, &, braces, `/`, `$`, line breaks); in expression position it is emitted as JSON - strings get quotes, numbers/booleans stay bare, maps/slices become objects/arrays. So write `var n = {{count}};` / `var cfg = {{cfg | json}};`, not `"{{x}}"` around a value you want as a number. A string-typed value in expression position (e.g. a query param) arrives as a JS string.

`{{{var}}}` and raw pipes (markdown) keep their unescaped HTML only in body text; in attributes and scripts they are escaped like `{{var}}`. `{{{{var}}}}` stays raw everywhere (explicit opt-out), except that a rendered value can never open a framework tag: `<query`, `<fetch` or `<transitions` followed by whitespace in a value renders as `<query ...` text. <script type="text/template"> and other non-JS types keep HTML escaping. engine: gotmpl uses html/template's own contextual escaping; the HTML/TSX stack's <include> pass does not evaluate mustache.

Layouts: `layout: <name>` (frontmatter, any engine) or `<page layout="<name>">` wraps the page in the mustache file layouts/<name>.html. The layout's own tags render over the page's render data ({{page_title}}, {{user_email}}, {{param_x}}, sections), then the finished page is written into its first `{{content}}` slot (`{{{content}}}` and `{{{{content}}}}` are the same slot) and is never scanned again, so a `{{...}}` that a gotmpl or raw page prints (from a URL parameter or a stored row, or for the layout to fill) shows as text: render the value in the page, or in the layout.
